Page 13 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology We further confirm the templated growth by characterizing the micro interface of the heterostructure using HRTEM. Figure 1.4 shows an epitaxial growth of 2D perovskites on 3D perovskites. By taking the FFT of the image, we identify 3D perovskite phases and 2D perovskite phases. We observed that the surface of the 3D perovskite is partly converted into a 2D perovskite phase. The 2D perovskites grow out of plane relative to the 3D perovskites, which can facilitate charge transfer from the 3D to 2D perovskite. Figure 1.4 HRTEM image of the templated 3D/2D interface We used photoluminance measurements to investigate the charge separation at the 3D/2D interface. By characterizing the novel heterostructure using power dependent photoluminescence, we found that the PL shifts to 810 nm for the novel 3D/2D heterostructure while the conventional treatment leads to a PL centered at 790 nm. Moreover, the increase of PL versus power has a slope ~ 1 while the bulk 3D perovskite has a slope of 1.44 in Figure 1.5. A power dependent slope of 1.44 in the control film indicates that the recombination is a mixture of free carrier bimolecular and monomolecular recombination. In Figure 1.6a and c, we illustrate that the conventional 2D, which has a type I alignment, blocks both types of carriers so that the majority of them recombine in the bulk perovskite. This mechanism is bimolecular. They can also get trapped and recombine through SRH mechanism which is monomolecular. The mixture of both leads to a power dependent PL slope between 1 and 2. However, in the templated 3D/2D structure, a power dependent slope of 1 indicates that the recombination is completely monomolecular. Our interpretation of this data is that the dominated recombination pathway in the novel heterostructure is interfacial recombination. As in Figure 1.6b and d, we believe a templated growth of 2D perovskite on 3D perovskite will allow a charge separation at the interface where one type of carrier will be selectively transferred into the 2D perovskites which leads to long carrier lifetime because of the decreased wavefunction overlap between electrons and holes. As one type of carrier Page 14 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology becomes the majority carrier at the interface, the recombination rate only depends on the diffusion of the other minority carrier (Figure 1.6 d). Thus, this process will be monomolecular. We conducted intensity dependent time-resoled photo- luminescence measurement (TRPL) to support the hypothesis.
